transcript:
Header: 2026-09-07 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Sophie Chen (Northbridge), Arjun Patel (Northbridge), Maya Rodriguez (Northbridge)

Summary: Quick Optimize walkthrough focused on batching and caching recommendations. Discussed prefix vs KV cache tradeoffs, cost model for tokens and GPU usage, recommended configs for hosted pilot vs dedicated pools, and next steps for a pilot benchmark and security docs.

Topics: batching strategy, KV cache sizing, prefix cache hits, per-token cost model, latency vs throughput, dedicated vs hosted, KMS/encryption, SOC2/audit logs

00:00 Lena: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this tight. I'm lena from Redwood, and marco is our SE who will run through the optimizer walkthrough. Sophie: thanks lena, excited, we've been thinking about the cost/latency tradeoff for our chat summarization workload.

02:18 Marco: okay quick context, northbridge is doing multi-turn summarization and reranking, average convo length ~18 turns, typical prompt prefix includes policy + user history ~1.2k tokens, and you mentioned p95 latency target of ~400ms; is that right sophie?

02:45 Sophie: yeah p95 around 350-400ms is ideal, we can tolerate some longer tails for longer histories but cost is a big driver for us. we process ~400k tokens/day currently in experiment.

05:12 Marco: cool. so the high-level levers we covered: batching (request-level batching / batching window), prefix caching vs KV cache, quantization level for model variants, and routing policies (hosted vs dedicated). i'll show a simple cost model: cost per token + GPU time because batching increases throughput but can increase tail latency.

07:05 Marco: first, prefix cache - that's when we cache the output of the prompt prefix or instruction embedding, so when you have repeated system messages or static instructions we can avoid re-encoding. it's lightweight and great for high hit rates, but doesn't help when the dynamic user history changes a lot.

08:40 Lena: we see prefix cache working well for your system prompt + policy text, which is very static. you should get a high hit rate there.

09:22 Arjun: quick question: how do you size the prefix cache, does it increase memory on the server a lot?

09:35 Marco: it's mostly an embedding/prefix KV with TTL; memory footprint is modest relative to KV cache. KV cache is a different story — that's the transformer KV- cache saved per sequence which can be large for long context and is kept per active session. KV cache saves autoregressive recomputation on subsequent calls and is high value for multi-turn back-and-forth.

10:40 Sophie: so prefix cache for static system prompts, KV for multi-turn speedup, got it. what's the rough cost delta?

11:02 Marco: in our model example: with no caching, assume 1.0x token compute. prefix cache alone might reduce avg token compute by ~5-15% depending on static proportion; KV cache can reduce generation compute by up to 40-70% on long sessions, because you skip early layers' recompute. combined with batching and quantization you can reduce per-token GPU time substantially.

13:30 Marco: i'll share a simplified cost table — example numbers for a 70B model on A100: baseline 100 tokens/s per GPU, cost $X/hr; with batching tuned (window 20ms), throughput improves 2.5x but p95 increases ~10-20ms. KV cache hit rate of 60% can cut token compute by ~45% leading to ~35-40% lower GPU hours. these are illustrative; we'll run your exact workload to get real numbers.

16:05 Maya: are there constraints for KV cache in hosted mode? we have data residency and some compliance needs.

16:20 Lena: good point. hosted supports per-customer isolation and configurable retention. for stricter compliance we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private where KV can be resident in your VPC. we also support KMS/HSM integration for keys.

17:10 Sophie: what about cache eviction and cold-starts? our users have long tail sessions, some months-old threads.

17:35 Marco: eviction policies are TTL-based + LRU. for very long-lived sessions you can pin sessions to dedicated workers or persist KV to a warm store (tradeoff: slightly higher latency on reload). We'll propose a policy based on your session distribution.

20:00 Arjun: can we get the specific config you'd recommend for our workload? like batching window, max batch size, prefix/kv TTLs and estimated cost impact?

20:20 Marco: yes — preliminary recommendation: batching window 15-25ms, max batch size 64 for low-latency tier; use prefix cache TTL 24h for policy text; KV cache TTL 7 days with hot eviction for active sessions. For a pilot hosted run, we suggest enabling prefix cache + KV caching with a 60% expected hit rate to estimate savings. i'll send the spreadsheet with scenario A (hosted) and B (dedicated).

24:12 Sophie: ok what about model variants: do you recommend quantized model for production? how does it impact accuracy?

24:35 Marco: quantization (8-bit / 4-bit) often gives decent perf tradeoffs. For your summarization workload we recommend testing 4-bit LLM variant in a canary — usually small quality delta, big throughput gains. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profiles per workload and rollback if evals show regressions.

26:50 Maya: network egress and per-token billing — will batching change our billing profile?

27:05 Lena: batching improves GPU efficiency so reduces GPU-hour based cost; per-token charges (hosted) remain but effective tokens processed per GPU hour increases so cost-per-token drops. we'll show side-by-side in the cost model spreadsheet.

29:10 Marco: also routing policies: you can route high-priority traffic to dedicated pool and burst to hosted for overflow. this helps meet p95 SLOs while optimizing costs.

31:00 Sophie: security — are audit logs and query-level redaction supported? we need to keep PII out of logs.

31:20 Marco: yes, we offer audit logs, configurable PII scrubbing, and can integrate with your SIEM. for private deployments we can keep logs on-prem. all encryption in transit and at rest, and we integrate with customer KMS.

33:40 Arjun: any obvious gotchas when we run the pilot? like cold start for KV or batch tail latencies?

34:00 Marco: main things to watch: tail latency from batch queuing (tune window), KV cold-starts when session is evicted, and mis-sized batch limits causing head-of-line issues. we'll instrument these in Redwood Console and alert on p95 regressions.

36:15 Lena: we'll include dashboard views for token costs, batch size distributions, cache hit rate, and a regression alert if quality drops >2% on your eval prompts.

38:40 Sophie: sounds good. can you run a sample benchmark against our anonymized workload on Monday? we'd like numbers to present to procurement.

38:55 Lena: yes monday works, marco will coordinate.

40:10 Marco: for the benchmark we'll need a ~24 hour sample or representative load (spike patterns), the model variant to test, and access method (hosted API keys or a dedicated test pool). Sophie, can you send the workload file and target SLOs?

40:35 Sophie: i'll share by EOD tomorrow.

42:20 Lena: recap of next steps: marco to send cost model + configs, lena to send pricing/SOW, northbridge to send workload + SLOs. we also agreed to run a 48-hour pilot with monitoring.

45:00 Maya: thanks everyone.

45:10 Lena: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs.

End of transcript. Links shared during call: [Redwood optimize cost model spreadsheet] (link), [SOC2 + KMS integration notes] (link), [pilot SOW template] (link).
